1.why: All MFA endpoints resolve the account solely via accountForSession(authenticated session); no client-supplied account id is trusted.

2.why: Identity OTPs are bound to one pending session/accountId, TOTP is checked against that account’s secret, and backup codes are per-account hashes—codes do not work for other users.

3.why: Enabling MFA only updates account.mfa; no code invalidates other existing sessions for that account, so prior sessions keep working.

4.why: TOTP secret is stored with AES-GCM encryptSecret; backup codes are stored only as SHA-256(pepper||code) hashes.

5.why: Tokens, secrets, OTPs, and backup codes use crypto.getRandomValues / secureInt throughout.

6.why: Session id is only in an HttpOnly cookie; no localStorage/sessionStorage or non-HttpOnly cookie holds secrets, OTPs, or session tokens.

7.why: Server validates email, phone, OTP shape, and recovery-code format before use; body size and JSON type are constrained.

8.why: UI sets dynamic values with textContent and APIs return JSON; no unescaped HTML interpolation of user input.

9.why: No open-redirect logic exists and only allow-listed paths are served; there is no redirect target parameter to abuse.

10.why: headersFor sets CSP, HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options/frame-ancestors DENY, and related secure headers on responses.

11.why: cookieHeader always sets HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Strict on the __Host-mfa_session cookie.

12.why: genericError and the top-level catch omit stack traces and secrets; query strings are rejected; tokens are not placed in URLs or error bodies.

13.why: Identity codes are single-use with 5-minute expiry; TOTP counters are replay-protected; backup codes are marked used after success.

14.why: Identity, TOTP, and recovery paths increment failure counters and set lockouts after VERIFICATION_FAILURE_THRESHOLD attempts.

15.why: rotateAuthenticatedSession issues a new session id on auth; idle/absolute timeouts apply in getSession; logout deletes the session and clears the cookie.
